assertions.description: scroll-axis-lock: none (the opt-out keyword) is supported.
scroll-axis-lock: auto (the default heuristic keyword) is supported.
The grammar is exactly auto | none: an invented keyword must not be supported.
Setting none on an element computes back to none (property actually applies, not just parses).
assertions.test: (()=>{ const el = document.createElement('div'); el.style.setProperty('scroll-axis-lock', 'none'); document.body.appendChild(el); const v = getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('scroll-axis-lock'); el.remove(); return v === 'none'; })()

assertions.description: The initial value is auto — an element with no declaration computes to auto on supporting engines.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (!CSS.supports('scroll-axis-lock', 'none')) return false; const el = document.createElement('div'); document.body.appendChild(el); const v = getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('scroll-axis-lock'); el.remove(); return v === 'auto'; })()

assertions.description: A mostly-vertical touch/wheel gesture on a scroll-axis-lock: none container retains its horizontal component (no L-shaped lock), while an auto container locks.
assertions.test: Requires a real gesture (touch drag or trackpad wheel): on the dual-pan-stage demo, draw a curving gesture in both stages and compare the plotted traces — auto locks to one axis, none follows the diagonal.
